claims.claim: Czechia now requires Russian diplomats to give at least one day’s notice of border crossings, including purpose, route, duration and places of stay.
claims.episode_span: notify Czech authorities at least one day before
claims.source_title: Democracy Digest: Czechia Restricts Rules for Russian Diplomats Travelling
claims.supporting_quote: According to the new regulations, Russian diplomatic personnel must now notify the Czech authorities of their plans to cross the border at least one day in advance, announce the purpose of their trip, as well as the precise route, duration and places of their stay.

claims.claim: Foreign Minister Petr Macinka called the Czech rule reciprocal and said European states are trying to limit movement by Russian intelligence officers.
claims.episode_span: Macinka called the change reciprocal
claims.source_title: Democracy Digest: Czechia Restricts Rules for Russian Diplomats Travelling
claims.supporting_quote: “I consider it an absolutely right step, because it is a reciprocal measure that the Russian Federation also applies to our diplomats,” Foreign Minister Macinka said.

claims.claim: Martin Kupka of ODS called the Czech measure a half-measure because Russian diplomats can still enter on Schengen visas.
claims.episode_span: called the step a half-measure
claims.source_title: Democracy Digest: Czechia Restricts Rules for Russian Diplomats Travelling
claims.supporting_quote: “We are still only halfway there. Russian diplomats can continue to travel to the Czech Republic on Schengen visas, and the Czech state cannot say ‘no’ to them,” said Martin Kupka, the head of the opposition right-wing ODS party.

claims.claim: The request came from the Office of the National Cyber Director, and the White House, Anthropic and OpenAI did not immediately comment.

claims.supporting_quote: The request came from the Office of the National Cyber Director. The White House wants to make sure US systems are secure before the models are shared with partners. The White House, Anthropic and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

claims.supporting_quote: He said the institute still had "pre-release access to some of the world's most capable models", and noted that it tested OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra before its public release.
